词汇 · 旅游语境
词汇 · 旅游语境 在语境中选择措辞

按给定条件改写，不添加数据。

作答条件：新公交服务开通后，旺季道路拥堵有所缓解但仍存在；旅游提供部分季节性岗位；现有信息不足以判定旅游的总收益大于总成本。

待改写段（自编）：Tourism inevitably eliminates unemployment. The new buses eradicated congestion. Therefore, its advantages outweigh than its disadvantages.

Revise the wording so that each claim matches the information available.

把待改写段写成 40–55 个英文词。保留三个信息：就业作用、交通变化、总利弊尚无法确定。

每空填一个合适的词：① Tourism can contribute ___ local employment. ② More visitors may put pressure ___ public services. ③ Whether the benefits outweigh the costs depends ___ how tourism is managed.

答案

1. 示例：Tourism can provide seasonal employment, although this does not eliminate unemployment. Congestion has eased since the new bus service began, but traffic problems remain. On the information given, it is not possible to conclude that the overall benefits of tourism outweigh its costs.
2. ① to；② on；③ on。

再练一次

用 30–45 个英文词回应：旅游收入增加就一定意味着居民生活改善吗？使用 may 或 can；不使用 inevitable、eradicate 或 impressive。

答案

示例：Higher tourism revenue may improve residents' lives if it supports stable jobs and better local services. However, an increase in business income alone does not show that residents benefit, especially where housing costs also rise.

TOPIC 04

城市：把住房、交通与公共空间放在一起看

城市生活涉及住在哪里、怎样出行，以及能否方便地使用学校、商店和公共空间。住房、交通与服务不能完全分开讨论：房子离工作地点多远，会影响出行安排；公园即使在附近，入口和开放时间也会影响使用。改善城市不只有新建道路这一种选择，还可讨论公共交通、步行条件和空间用途。不同居民的预算、行动条件与日常目的地可能不同。

先分清三个概念

概念它指什么不要混淆
public transport供公众共同使用的交通服务，例如公共汽车、地铁和有轨电车。有线路经过与服务方便可靠不是一回事；站点位置、班次和不同线路之间的连接都影响使用。
housing affordability住房支出与个人或家庭能够承担的预算之间的关系。价格低不一定对每个人都负担得起；判断时还需考虑收入以及其他必要生活支出。
public space供公众进入或共同使用的空间，例如广场、公园和部分街道空间。公共空间不一定是绿地；有一片绿地也不代表公众能够进入或方便使用。

读一段背景英语

A city is more than a collection of buildings. It also connects people with the places they need to reach. Consider a family looking for a home. The rent matters, but so do the distance to work, the route to school and the shops nearby. A flat outside the centre may suit them if transport fits their daily schedule. A park can be useful too, but its entrances and opening hours affect who can use it. These examples show why planning involves choices about both space and services. Different residents may have different priorities. A useful discussion of city life can describe a particular need and then consider how a change would affect the people who live there.
中文帮助理解

城市不仅是建筑的集合，也把居民与日常需要到达的地方连接起来。一个家庭选择住房时，除了租金，还可能考虑工作地点、上学路线和附近商店。市中心以外的住宅是否合适，要看交通能否配合他们的生活安排。公园能否实际使用，也与入口和开放时间有关。因此，城市规划既涉及空间，也涉及服务；不同居民重视的条件不尽相同。具体讨论某类人的需要，再解释一项变化会怎样影响他们，比笼统说城市应更方便更清楚。

阅读例句

Vehicles can be flowing freely along, at a density still well below what the road can handle, and then suddenly gel into a slow-moving ooze.

原文讨论车流的变化。交通容量、交通流量和实际通行速度不是同一指标。

The Physics of Traffic Behavior

这个话题通常怎样展开

以下为教学归纳的讨论角度，不是考试频率排名或原题清单。

  • 居民选择居住地点时，怎样权衡住房成本、交通和附近服务？（教学概括，非原题）
  • 城市应怎样分配道路、步行区域与公共空间？（教学概括，非原题）
  • 改善公共交通时，票价、班次、路线和可靠性分别影响什么？（教学概括，非原题）

可以直接理解和借用的搭配

本组是教学选用搭配与例句，尚未逐组统计真题频率。

搭配与意思放进句子里
use public transport
使用公共交通		He uses public transport to get to work during the week.
within walking distance of
位于从某地步行可达的距离内		The library is within walking distance of the bus station.
meet housing needs
满足住房需要		The plan needs to consider how to meet the housing needs of different households.
provide green spaces
提供绿地空间		A neighbourhood plan can provide green spaces for residents to use.
travel to and from work
往返工作地点，通勤		Residents may need to change buses when they travel to and from work.

读过背景后，需要练习时再进入：阅读章 · Task 1 · 口语章。已读过原句或提示的任务，记为学习后应用。

这部分怎样放进每天的学习

每次只选一段：先用 8–12 分钟读懂背景，再花 3–5 分钟看两三组表达。时间计入当天学习，不在原计划之外加量。熟悉的段落直接跳过；累时读懂一段即可。

听读时，关注同一意思怎样换说法、句间关系与证据；写作时，重新核对题目问了什么、理由适用于什么条件；口语时，选自己的具体经历，练习把人、地点、变化和结果说清楚。阅读记录与写作稿继续分别保存。

隔天只抽两组表达：遮住英语，换一个真实场景说或写一句；能独立用且意思合适，再减少复习。用新语境中的独立表达检查掌握情况，例句记忆与实际运用分别记录。

TOPIC 01

教育：谁能学到，学什么，怎样学

教育讨论常围绕三个问题：谁有机会接受教育，课程应包含什么，以及怎样判断学习成果。能进入学校，不等于能获得适合自己的帮助；考试成绩也只是学习表现的一部分。学术知识、实际技能和独立思考可以相互支持，不必选一个就放弃另一个。讨论统一课程与个别支持时，还要考虑教师时间、学生起点，以及学校能提供哪些资源。

先分清三个概念

概念它指什么不要混淆
access to education获得教育机会，包括能够入学、参与课程并使用必要的学习资源。有机会进入课程与实际学懂是两件事；提供一个学习名额并不自动解决时间、语言或学习支持问题。
practical skills能够用于具体活动或解决实际问题的技能，例如操作工具、安排任务和处理信息。实际技能不只指手工或职业技术；它也可以用到学科知识，不能简单理解成与理论相反。
equal opportunity让不同背景的学习者有公平参与和发展的机会。公平机会不一定意味着每个人得到完全相同的帮助；起点不同的人可能需要不同程度的支持。

读一段背景英语

A school has several purposes. It can introduce students to knowledge, help them develop useful skills and give them experience of working with others. These purposes do not always require separate lessons. A science project, for example, can involve reading, measuring and explaining a result to a partner. However, students may need different kinds of support to take part. One student may understand the subject but struggle with the language used in class. Another may need more time to practise a skill. A common curriculum can give a class shared goals, while additional support can help students work towards them. When discussing education, it is useful to consider both what schools expect and what learners need.
中文帮助理解

把教育概念用到具体问题里

先用两个课堂情境检查理解，再看一道正式写作题怎样限定讨论范围。前两题是本册编写的理解练习。

  1. 两名学生都能参加科学项目。甲会测量，但听不懂课堂指令；乙能理解指令，却需要练习测量。给两人同一份作业是否就满足了各自的学习需要？各写一种帮助，并说明帮助解决的困难。
  2. 学校给所有学生安排相同的项目目标，同时为需要的学生提供双语词表和额外练习时间。这属于改变学习目标，还是改变参与方式？用 access to education 和 equal opportunity 解释：已有名额，还缺什么？
完成后核对

① 甲需要理解指令的支持，例如关键术语表或一次演示；乙需要测量练习和反馈。两人都能入学，不代表都已获得适合的支持。② 目标相同，支持方式不同；平等机会可以通过不同帮助实现，不必把“公平”理解成每个人得到完全一样的东西。具体措施还受教师时间与可用资源限制。

正式题：小学课堂的正式学习与游戏

Some people argue that primary schools focus too much on formal learning.
To what extent do you agree with this opinion?
How important do you think it is for children to play as well as learn in the primary school classroom?

原题要求说明理由并举相关例子，完整作文至少 250 词，建议 40 分钟。本次只练审题与一个理由段，不计作完成整篇作文。

  1. 写出题目中的两项要求，并明确讨论对象与场景。
  2. 设计一个课堂活动，说明孩子在其中学什么、怎样参与、为什么需要游戏。再补一句：什么情况下需要额外的学习支持？
完成后核对

两项要求分别是：是否同意小学过于重视正式学习；游戏在小学课堂里有多重要。范围是小学课堂，不能只讨论大学就业或入学机会。

原创示例：A simple shop game can help children practise addition while taking turns as customers and shopkeepers. They use numbers for a clear purpose and learn to cooperate. A child who struggles with the instructions may need a demonstration before joining in. 这里“游戏—计算与合作—示范支持”逐项对应 practical skills 和 learners’ needs；它是理由段示例，没有官方分数。

打开同题考生稿：找出第 2 段支持正式学习的两点，以及第 3 段说明游戏价值的两点。再读评语，修改自己段落里最笼统的一句。

核对：考生稿谈到纪律与尊重、考试检验学习；游戏段谈到社交与创造技能、减少无聊并激发长期学习兴趣。考官认可回应两问和相关展开，同时指出结论笼统、句首连接词过多，以及个别搭配错误。7.5 分属于这份考生原稿，并不说明其中每句话都值得照抄。

A Chronicle of Timekeeping Our conception of time depends on the way we measure it A According to archaeological evidence, at least 5,000 years ago, and long before the advent of the Roman Empire, the Babylonians began to measure time, introducing calendars to co- ordinate communal activities, to plan the shipment of goods and, in particular, to regulate planting and harvesting. They based their calendars on three natural cycles: the solar day, marked by the successive periods of light and darkness as the earth rotates on its axis; the lunar month, following the phases of the moon as it orbits the earth; and the solar year, deﬁ ned by the changing seasons that accompany our planet’s revolution around the sun. B Before the invention of artiﬁ cial light, the moon had greater social impact. And, for those living near the equator in particular, its waxing and waning was more conspicuous than the passing of the seasons. Hence, the calendars that were developed at the lower latitudes were inﬂ uenced more by the lunar cycle than by the solar year. In more northern climes, however, where seasonal agriculture was practised, the solar year became more crucial. As the Roman Empire expanded northward, it organised its activity chart for the most part around the solar year. C Centuries before the Roman Empire, the Egyptians had formulated a municipal calendar having 12 months of 30 days, with ﬁ ve days added to approximate the solar year. Each period of ten days was marked by the appearance of special groups of stars called decans. At the rise of the star Sirius just before sunrise, which occurred around the all- important annual ﬂ ooding of the Nile, 12 decans could be seen spanning the heavens. The cosmic signiﬁ cance the Egyptians placed in the 12 decans led them to develop a system in which each interval of darkness (and later, each interval of daylight) was divided into a dozen equal parts. These periods became known as temporal hours because their duration varied according to the changing length of days and nights with the passing of the seasons. D In order to track temporal hours during the day, inventors created sundials, which indicate time by the length or direction of the sun’s shadow. The sundial’s counterpart, the water clock, was designed to measure temporal hours at night. One of the ﬁ rst water clocks was a basin with a small hole near the bottom through which the water dripped out. The falling water level denoted the passing hour as it dipped below hour lines inscribed on the inner surface. Although these devices performed satisfactorily around the Mediterranean, they could not always be depended on in the cloudy and often freezing weather of northern Europe. E The advent of the mechanical clock meant that although it could be adjusted to maintain temporal hours, it was naturally suited to keeping equal ones. With these, however, arose the question of when to begin counting, and so, in the early 14th century, a number of systems evolved. The schemes that divided the day into 24 equal parts varied according to the start of the count: Italian hours began at sunset, Babylonian hours at sunrise, astronomical hours at midday and ‘great clock’ hours, used for some large public clocks in Germany, at midnight. Eventually these were superseded by ‘small clock’, or French, hours, which split the day into two 12- hour periods commencing at midnight. F The earliest recorded weight - driven mechanical clock was built in 1283 in Bedfordshire in England. The revolutionary aspect of this new timekeeper was neither the descending weight that provided its motive force nor the gear wheels (which had been around for at least 1,300 years) that transferred the power; it was the part called the escapement. In the early 1400s came the invention of the coiled spring or fusee which maintained constant force to the gear wheels of the timekeeper despite the changing tension of its mainspring. By the 16th century, a pendulum clock had been devised, but the pendulum swung in a large arc and thus was not very efﬁ cient. G To address this, a variation on the original escapement was invented in 1670, in England. It was called the anchor escapement, which was a lever- based device shaped like a ship’s anchor. The motion of a pendulum rocks this device so that it catches and then releases each tooth of the escape wheel, in turn allowing it to turn a precise amount. Unlike the original form used in early pendulum clocks, the anchor escapement permitted the pendulum to travel in a very small arc. Moreover, this invention allowed the use of a long pendulum which could beat once a second and thus led to the development of a new ﬂ oor- standing case design, which became known as the grandfather clock. H Today, highly accurate timekeeping instruments set the beat for most electronic devices. Nearly all computers contain a quartz- crystal clock to regulate their operation. Moreover, not only do time signals beamed down from Global Positioning System satellites calibrate the functions of precision navigation equipment, they do so as well for mobile phones, instant stock- trading systems and nationwide power- distribution grids.
